beats.narration: Six thousand years ago, the Sahara had lakes — hippos in the water, giraffes painted on its rocks.
beats.claim: the Sahara hosted lakes and wetland fauna ~6,000 years ago
beats.visual_question: how could a desert have hippos?
beats.visual_answer: a dawn lakescape — hippos at the waterline under acacias, full-bleed

beats.narration: The rock art is still there: swimming figures, cattle herds, giraffes — drawn where nothing survives today.
beats.claim: 15,000+ rock-art panels across the Sahara record wetland life
beats.visual_answer: an ochre rock-art panel on desert sandstone — the record itself

beats.narration: Today the desert's heart gets under 25 millimeters of rain a year. Back then, monsoons fed grasslands and vast lakes.
beats.claim: African Humid Period: monsoon-fed lakes vs today's hyperarid core
beats.visual_answer: split plate: green lake shore on one side, the same land cracked dry on the other

beats.narration: The switch is the Earth itself: its axis wobbles on a 26,000-year cycle, dragging the monsoon north — then letting it go.
beats.claim: axial precession (~26,000-year cycle) paces the North African monsoon
beats.visual_answer: a parchment diagram: tilted Earth, axis wobble, the monsoon belt moving north

beats.narration: The green age ended fast: around 5,500 years ago the rains withdrew within centuries, and people drifted toward the Nile.
beats.claim: the humid period ended ~5,500 BP within centuries, driving migration to the Nile
beats.visual_answer: a cracked dry lakebed where the lake was — the end of the green age

beats.narration: Six thousand years of rain, paused — not erased.
beats.claim: green Sahara episodes recur, paced by orbital cycles
beats.visual_answer: the type card states it: IT WAS GREEN

beats.narration: The link still lives: each year the desert lifts about 180 million tons of dust — 27 million tons lands on the Amazon, fertilizer from a green world.
beats.claim: Saharan dust fertilizes the Amazon (~27 Mt/yr)
beats.visual_answer: satellite view: an orange dust plume crossing the Atlantic from Africa
